0x1485c: takes a cue index and a second long, rejects any index above 22 by returning 0xFF, and otherwise reads a word from the table at 0x1D616 to drive the sequencer. It holds 0x3E34CC in a2, 0x3E3536 in a4 and 0x143B0 in a3 - and 0x3E34CC is the pointer the goal statement names as being stored at 0x3E3268 and 0x3E3288 around frame 276, so this is the routine at the centre of that. Reached through the trampoline at 0x18A. 474 bytes; read the head at 0x1485C-0x1489E.
0xe546: pushes 0 and 0x13 and calls the sound-cue starter through the trampoline at 0x18A. Nothing else - a named shorthand for one cue. Read at 0xE546-0xE554.
0xe554: the same as 0xE546 with 0x12 instead of 0x13. Read at 0xE554-0xE562.
0x1867c: jump through the slot only if it holds a trampoline

takes a pointer and compares the word there against 0x4EF9, the encoding of `jmp <abs>.l`. If it matches it jumps to that address; otherwise it returns zero without calling anything. 0x4EF9 is exactly the signature describe.py uses to find the trampoline block below the first routine, so this is a guarded dispatch: the slot is only entered when it really does hold a jump stub. Read at 0x1867C-0x1868C.
0xfb74: return the argument as a pointer

one move and an rts, returning the first stack argument in a0. The map's twelve-byte extent covers a second identical fragment at 0x0FB7A, so the run is two copies of the same two instructions. Read at 0x0FB74-0x0FB80.
0x122b2: decoder state: emit d0, then d3

writes d0 to the destination and points a2 at 0x122BC. The whole-byte counterpart of the nibble pair at 0x1228C/0x1229E - same two-state machine held in a2, but emitting two registers in turn rather than splitting one byte. Read at 0x122B2-0x122BC.
0x122bc: decoder state: emit d3, then d0
the other half of 0x122B2: writes d3 and points a2 back. Read at 0x122BC-0x122C6.
0x17ed4: a shared epilogue: movem.l from -0x24(a6) into d2-d6 and a2-a4, unlk a6, rts. The larger sibling of 0x7866, which restores only d2 and a2. Routines jump here to return. Read at 0x17ED4-0x17EDE.
0x19c00: fill bytes with a long count

memset. Fills count+1 bytes at the pointer with the given byte and returns the original pointer, using the same dbra plus `subi.l #$10000` extension as the copy at 0x19BC2 so the count can exceed 65,535. Read at 0x19C00-0x19C22.
0x19c22: set the status register and return the old one

reads the status register into d0, writes the word it was given into it, and returns the previous value - the save-and-restore primitive for the interrupt mask, and the routine that raises or lowers it. Worth noting against 0x15A0, which carried the name 'interrupt mask set' until 2026-07-31 and does nothing of the kind: it ORs and ANDs a word in work RAM. This is the one that touches the mask. Read at 0x19C22-0x19C2E.
0x1868c: strlen. Scans forward from the pointer it is given until it reads a zero byte, then returns the distance minus one. The minus one is `moveq #$ff,d0`, which sign-extends to -1 rather than loading 255 - read it as 255 and the routine looks like it returns the length plus 256. Read at 0x1868C-0x1869E.
0x19bc2: copy bytes with a long count

a byte copy whose count is a full long, not a word: dbra handles the low sixteen bits and `subi.l #$10000` with a bcc repeats that for each higher unit, which is the standard way to run a dbra loop past 65,535. Read at 0x19BC2-0x19BD8.
0x197d8: divide a long by a word

the 68000's divu only takes a 32-bit dividend and gives a 16-bit quotient, so this does it in two halves - divide the high word, keep the remainder in place, divide the low - and negates the result when a0 is negative. Read at 0x197D8-0x197F4.
0x1940a: clear an eight-kilobyte band of the playfield

takes a byte, shifts it left twelve (swap then lsr.l #4, which is how the 68000 gets a sixteen-bit shift cheaply), adds that to 0x200004 and clears 0x800 longs from there - eight kilobytes, sixteen playfield rows at the 0x200 stride. Read at 0x1940A-0x1942A.
0x1865e: save the machine state for a later jump

setjmp. Takes a buffer pointer, reads the return address off the stack into d1, and movem.l's d1-d7 and a2-a7 into the buffer - so the buffer holds every callee-saved register plus where to come back to. Returns zero, which is the first-time return. Its partner is 0x1866C. Read at 0x1865E-0x1866C.
0x1866c: restore a saved state and jump back

longjmp. Takes the buffer 0x1865E filled and a value, movem.l's the registers back out of it, and writes the saved return address over the one on the stack so the rts lands in the original caller instead of this one. The value it was given is already in d0 and becomes that return's result. Read at 0x1866C-0x1867C.
0x17ede: wait until the long at 0x3E3532 changes

reads 0x3E3532, then compares it against itself in a loop, spinning while equal - so it blocks until something outside changes that long - and then calls 0x19C3C. A second wait distinct from the frame semaphore at 0x3E0802 that 0x512 uses. Read at 0x17EDE-0x17EF4.
0x160dc: takes a pointer and returns the bitwise or of the bytes at offsets 0, 1 and 2, zero-extended. Read at 0x160DC-0x160F8.
0x1228c: decoder state: emit the high nibble, then the low

fetches the next source byte, writes its high nibble plus d2 to the destination, and leaves a2 pointing at 0x1229E. The decompressor keeps its state in that register rather than in a variable: each state ends by naming its successor, and the caller jumps through a2. This is the `lea $X(pc),aN` continuation shape CLAUDE.md flags, and it is why each state needs its own decompiled function. Read at 0x1228C-0x1229E.
0x1229e: decoder state: emit the low nibble, then the high

the other half of 0x1228C. Writes the low nibble of the byte already fetched, plus d2, and points a2 back at 0x1228C so the next call fetches again. Two states alternating gives one byte per two output pixels. Read at 0x1229E-0x122AE.
0x1232e: second decoder state: emit the high nibble, then the low

the same alternation as 0x1228C over a different register set - source a3, byte d7, bias a5, continuation a4 - so the decompressor has two independent instances of the state machine. Read at 0x1232E-0x12340.
0x12340: second decoder state: emit the low nibble, then the high

the partner of 0x1232E, writing the low nibble of d7 plus a5 and pointing a4 back. Note the map's extent runs two instructions past the rts into 0x12350, which stores d4 and returns - a third fragment sharing the range. Read at 0x12340-0x12354.
0xf2ee: pointer from an offset into the record table
adds 0x1F7F0 to its argument, the exact inverse of 0xF2FA which subtracts it. Offset in, pointer out. Read at 0xF2EE-0xF2FA.
0x12066: shift eight pixels' colour by a delta

takes a pointer in a1 and a delta in d0, and for eight consecutive bytes replaces each with its low nibble plus the delta. Register arguments, no stack frame - an inner helper of 0x1204C. Read at 0x12066-0x12078.
0x1204c: shift an eight by two block's colour

calls 0x12066 on the pointer it is given and again 0x1F8 further on. 0x1F8 plus the eight bytes 0x12066 walks is 0x200, the playfield row stride, so this recolours two rows of eight pixels - an eight by two block. Read at 0x1204C-0x12066.
0xfc10: tst.w on 0x140000 and tst.l on 0x1432B0, both inside the window CLAUDE.md records as served by a state machine rather than plain memory. It keeps neither value; only the reads and the flags they leave. Compare 0xFC06, which reads 0x1400E8. Read at 0xFC10-0xFC1E.
0xe776: look up the value paired with a byte

walks the table at 0x11A90 a byte at a time until it finds one equal to the argument, then returns the byte after it. The table is therefore key/value pairs, and there is no bound on the search - a key that is not present runs off the end, so the table must be terminated by something the caller can only ever ask for. Read at 0xE776-0xE790.
0xe790: look up the byte paired with a value

the inverse of 0xE776 over the same table: starts one byte later at 0x11A91, scans for a match, and returns the byte before it. So 0xE776 maps key to value and this maps value back to key. Read at 0xE790-0xE7A8.
0xea68: work out and store the carry-over flag

passes its argument to 0xEA7A and stores the byte that comes back at 0x3E1956. That is the flag 0x1836 tests when deciding whether to skip one player during the new-game reset - the mechanism that carries a player over instead of wiping them. Read at 0xEA68-0xEA7A.
0xee22: translate one byte through the board table
reads the byte at 0x3E0DD2, uses it to index the table at 0x140034 in the board data region, and stores the result at 0x3E0DD4. A single translation between two globals. Read at 0xEE22-0xEE3A.
0xc4ca: link a node into the list after another

a doubly-linked list insert. Takes the node to insert and the node to insert after: saves the second's successor, points it at the new node, sets the new node's back link, gives it the saved successor, and fixes that successor's back link. So the links are next at offset 4 and previous at offset 0. Read at 0xC4CA-0xC4E8.
0xc1ee: find a free two-byte slot marked by a high bit

walks thirty-two two-byte slots from 0x3E1C44 and returns the first whose byte is negative, or null when none is (suba.l a0,a0). Note the convention differs from 0xB2B0 and 0xB2CC, where free means a zero long at offset 4: here it is the high bit of the first byte being set. Read at 0xC1EE-0xC206.
0xdabc: copy 1344 bytes and return the count
takes a source and a destination and moves 0x540 bytes one at a time with a dbra over 0x53F, counting as it goes and returning the count. Read at 0xDABC-0xDAD6.
0xb2cc: find a free slot in the moving-unit table

walks seven eighteen-byte slots from 0x3E1BC6 - the moving-unit table - and returns the address of the first whose long at offset 4 is zero, or null when every slot is taken (suba.l a0,a0 zeroes the register). So a long at +4 of zero means free. Read at 0xB2CC-0xB2E8.
0xb2b0: find a free fourteen-byte slot past the player structs

the same shape as 0xB2CC one table along: sixteen fourteen-byte slots from 0x3E1AE6, returning the first whose long at offset 4 is zero, or null when all are taken. 0x3E1AE6 sits just past the player structs, which end at 0x3E1AE2. Read at 0xB2B0-0xB2CC.
0x5dec: one move and an rts: returns the long at 0xC(a7), the third argument. Note the map gives this an eighteen-byte extent covering two more fragments of the same kind - 0x5DF2 returns the second argument and 0x5DF8 the first - so the run is three tiny accessors sharing one entry. Read at 0x5DEC-0x5DFE.
0x7866: restore d2 and a2 and unlink
a shared epilogue: movem.l from -0xC(a6) into d2 and a2, unlk a6, rts. No work of its own - routines jump here to return. Read at 0x7866-0x7870.
0x3e26: clear the sixteen-slot table and its flag

clears the first long of each of sixteen eight-byte slots from 0x3E0DF6 (dbra over 16, stepping a0 by 8), then clears the flag byte at 0x3E0E78 that 0x3F10 sets and 0x3F1A clears. Read at 0x3E26-0x3E3E.
0x3f10: one instruction: stores 1 in the byte at 0x3E0E78. The counterpart of 0x3F1A, which clears it; 0x3E26 also clears it after wiping the table at 0x3E0DF6. Read at 0x3F10-0x3F1A.
0x3f1a: one instruction: clears the byte at 0x3E0E78, the flag 0x3F10 raises. Read at 0x3F1A-0x3F22.
0x46c2: calls 0xC832 - a palette writer - with five constant arguments, 0, 1, 12, 7 and 2, and nothing else. No parameters and no state, so it writes the same entry every time. Read at 0x46C2-0x46E0.
0x4f8c: takes a source and a destination on the stack and moves sixteen words - thirty-two bytes - from one to the other with a dbra loop. No interpretation of the contents. Read at 0x4F8C-0x4F9E.
0x545a: read field six of the current record, or zero
tests the pointer at 0x3E0EC2 and, if it is not null, returns the word at offset 6 of the record it points to; returns zero when the pointer is null. A guarded accessor. Read at 0x545A-0x5474.
0x15be: reset a record and arm it with five

takes a record pointer on the stack, clears the long at 0x4 and the bytes at 0x19 and 0x1D, then stores 5 in byte 0x21. Byte 0x1D is the same field 0x1F60 counts down, so this is the record's initial state. Read at 0x15BE-0x15D6.
0x1f60: takes a record pointer and decrements its byte at 0x1D unless that byte is already zero (bls, so unsigned). The field 0x15BE clears when it resets the record. Read at 0x1F60-0x1F70.
0x1f70: step the record's state down from four

takes a record pointer and decrements its byte at 0x1E only when that byte is exactly 4, leaving every other value alone - so it moves one specific state on and is a no-op otherwise. Read at 0x1F70-0x1F82.
0x37d2: blit one fixed graphic to the playfield

calls 0x12078 with two constant arguments: the source 0xBB38A in the image and the destination 0x200004, four bytes into the playfield. No parameters and no state - it draws the same thing to the same place every time. Read at 0x37D2-0x37E8.
0x512: zeroes the word at 0x3E0802, spins until it becomes non-zero, then decrements it and returns. 0x3E0802 is the frame semaphore the interrupt handler sets - the same one CLAUDE.md names in the spin-loop seam - so this is the game's frame wait. Read at 0x512-0x52A.
0x52a: one instruction: writes zero to the frame semaphore at 0x3E0802, without waiting. The bare counterpart of 0x512. Read at 0x52A-0x534.
0x156c: set bits in the second flag word
takes a word on the stack and ORs it into 0x3E0DC8 - a second flag word beside the one at 0x3E0DC6 that 0x1578 and 0x1592 serve. Read at 0x156C-0x1578.
0x1584: clear bits in the second flag word
takes a word on the stack, inverts it, and ANDs it into 0x3E0DC8. Exact counterpart of 0x156C, and the same pairing 0x1578/0x1592 have for 0x3E0DC6. Read at 0x1584-0x1592.
0x618: one instruction: clears the byte at 0x72FFFF. That is the watchdog the board resets by being written to - system.ts names it at 0x72FFFE and treats reads and writes across it as on-map for exactly this reason. Read at 0x618-0x620.
0xfc06: test a word in the protection window

one instruction: tst.w on 0x1400E8, which lies in the window CLAUDE.md records as served by a state machine rather than plain memory - the protection probe's two halves sit at 0x140010 and 0x1400E4. The routine only sets the flags from it; the caller acts on them. Read at 0xFC06-0xFC0E.
0x1578: set bits in the flag word
takes a word on the stack and ORs it into the flag word at 0x3E0DC6. Three instructions. Read at 0x1578-0x1584.
0x1592: clear bits in the flag word
takes a word on the stack, inverts it, and ANDs it into the flag word at 0x3E0DC6 - the exact counterpart of 0x1578. Read at 0x1592-0x15A0.
0x15a0: clear the two high flag bits and set the next

calls 0x1592 with 0x6000 to clear those two bits of the word at 0x3E0DC6, then 0x1578 with 0x1000 to set that one. Renamed 2026-07-31 from 'interrupt mask set', which was wrong: the 68000's interrupt mask lives in the status register, and this touches a word in work RAM. Bits 13 and 14 are alternatives to bit 12 in whatever that word selects. Read at 0x15A0-0x15B4.
0xf2fa: offset from the record table base
three instructions: takes a longword on the stack and returns it minus 0x1F7F0, turning a pointer into a record's own table into an offset from that table's base. Read at 0xF2FA-0xF306.
0x512a: clear the index in every player's object

walks all three structs at 0x3E1968, stride 0x7E - with no active check, unlike every other walk here - and for each follows the pointer at field 0x42, stores a word at its start and ORs 0x20 into its byte 2. The word comes from calling 0xF2FA on 0x1F7F0, and 0xF2FA subtracts 0x1F7F0, so the value is exactly zero: the index is being reset rather than set. Field 0x42 therefore points at a per-player object whose first word is an offset into the table at 0x1F7F0. Read at 0x512A-0x5168.
0x482e: gather the stations nobody is playing

walks the three structs at 0x3E1968, stride 0x7E, and acts on the ones whose field 0 has bit 15 CLEAR - the inverse of every other walk here, so this is about stations that are not in play. For each it copies a byte from the table at 0xFE03 and one from 0xFE07 into a pair at 0x3E1CA6/0x3E1CA7, advancing that destination only for unjoined stations so the result is compacted, then calls 0x48AE. Read at 0x482E-0x4880.
0x4a6a: walks the three structs at 0x3E1968, stride 0x7E, and for each whose field 0 has bits 14/15 set calls 0xC688 - the routine that writes the palette - passing the table at 0xFE18, the constants 13, 4, 3 and 4, and an index that runs 5, 6, 7, one per station. So each player gets its own palette entries. Read at 0x4A6A-0x4AB8.
0x1c34: run the player flag handler for every active player

walks the three structs at 0x3E1968, stride 0x7E, and calls 0x5948 - the player flag handler - with each one whose field 0 has bit 15 set. Nothing else. Note the gate is bit 15 alone, where 0x1836 and 0x18FA test bits 14 and 15 together, so this runs for a strictly wider set of players than those do. Read at 0x1C34-0x1C66.
0x149a: does this board cell belong to the player

takes a player struct and a coordinate pair on the stack. Reads the player number from field 0x2, indexes the owner-code table at 0x1000A with it, turns the coordinate into a board cell address through 0x11BD8 (cell address), masks the cell's owner bits with 0xC0, and returns all-ones when they match the player's code and zero when they do not. This is what settles the coordinate pair at fields 0x46/0x47: it is a board cell, and 0x18FA is looking for a starting cell the player already owns. Read at 0x149A-0x14DC.
0x18fa: walks the three structs at 0x3E1968, stride 0x7E, skipping any whose field 0 lacks bits 14/15. Copies the byte pair at fields 0x48/0x49 into a local, offers it to 0x149A together with the struct, and if that returns non-zero writes the pair into fields 0x46/0x47; otherwise it takes the next pair from the list pointed to by field 0x4A, stepping two bytes at a time, and tries again. 0x46/0x47 is therefore a coordinate pair - the same one 0x1980 writes out scaled by 64 through the pointers at 0x5E and 0x62, whose default 0x19D8 sets to 40. Read at 0x18FA-0x1980.
0x1836: reset the players for a new game

walks the three structs at 0x3E1968, stride 0x7E. For each it points field 0x6A at the shot rings (0x3E0F48), clears the ring's first two bytes and marks it 0xFF, and clears byte 0x16 - the value averaged by 0x1A70 - then, if field 0 has bits 14/15 set, clears byte 0x14 (the round), word 0x56 and long 0x28 and calls 0x5948 with the struct. The reset is skipped for the player whose address matches the pointer at 0x3E1C84 when the flag at 0x3E1956 is set, which is how one player is carried over. Read at 0x1836-0x18A6.
0x19d8: reset the player pair to forty

takes a player struct as a stack argument and writes the word 40 through both of its pointers, fields 0x5E and 0x62. It is the default arm of 0x1980, which writes byte 0x46 shifted left six through 0x5E and byte 0x47 the same way through 0x62 when its flag is set. So the two locations hold a paired per-player value that is either derived from 0x46/0x47 or reset to 40; what they mean is still unread. Read at 0x19D8-0x19EE.
0x5e0a: takes a player struct as a stack argument; reads byte 0x2 - the player number, which 0x2248 sets from the loop index - scales it by 128 (asl #6 then doubled), adds it to 0x3E1F1C to pick that player's block, writes 0xFF at the block's first byte, and stores the pointer both at 0x3E209C and in the struct's field 0x66. Read at 0x5E0A-0x5E38.
0x2248: walks the three structs at 0x3E1968, stride 0x7E, and resets each: clears field 0 (which holds the active bit 15), byte 0x2 and long 0x24; stores the pointers 0x3E080C into 0x5E, 0x3E0814 into 0x62 and 0x3E1888 into 0x7A; calls 0x5E0A with the struct and 0x5B4 with the index; and fills bytes from 0x3E0DCE with 0xFF as it goes. This is where 0x01980's per-player pointers come from. Read at 0x2248-0x22BA.
0x19ee: advance every active player to the next round

walks the three player structs at 0x3E1968, stride 0x7E, skipping any whose field 0 lacks bit 15. For each one: sets byte 0x15 to byte 0x14 plus one; if byte 0x1F is still zero - a player who has not played a round yet - also adds the result of 0x1A70, so someone joining an in-progress game starts near the others rather than at one; then increments 0x1F, clears 0x1C, adds 0x15 into the counter at 0x3E1CAA, and calls 0x5B16 with the player. Read at 0x19EE-0x1A5C.
0x1a70: walks all three player structs from 0x3E1968 at stride 0x7E, skipping any whose field 0 has bit 15 clear or whose byte at 0x1F is zero; sums byte 0x16 across the rest and halves it (asr.l #1). Read at 0x1A70-0x1AEA.
